item.research_question: Can high-entropy solid solutions be formed in non-oxide ceramic metal diborides with a hexagonal layered structure, and do they exhibit superior hardness and oxidation resistance compared to their constituent individual diborides?
item.material_system: Seven equimolar five-component metal diborides: (Hf0.2Zr0.2Ta0.2Nb0.2Ti0.2)B2, (Hf0.2Zr0.2Ta0.2Mo0.2Ti0.2)B2, (Hf0.2Zr0.2Mo0.2Nb0.2Ti0.2)B2, (Hf0.2Mo0.2Ta0.2Nb0.2Ti0.2)B2, (Mo0.2Zr0.2Ta0.2Nb0.2Ti0.2)B2, (Hf0.2Zr0.2Ta0.2Cr0.2Ti0.2)B2, and (Hf0.2Zr0.2W0.2Mo0.2Ti0.2)B2
item.processing_route: High-energy ball milling (HEBM) for 6 hours in WC media with 60-minute milling/5-minute cooling cycles, followed by spark plasma sintering (SPS) at 2000 °C for 5 minutes under 30 MPa pressure in vacuum (10^-2 Torr)
item.test_conditions: Hardness measured via Vickers indentation at 200 kgf/mm2 with 15s hold time; oxidation resistance assessed via sequential isothermal annealing in flowing dry air at 800–1500 °C for 1 hour per step
key_findings: Six of the seven compositions formed a single-phase hexagonal AlB2 structure with greater than 92% of theoretical density.
Aberration-corrected STEM confirmed 2-D high-entropy metal layers separated by rigid boron nets with no detectable layered segregation along the c-axis.
The measured standard deviations of lattice spacings between basal (0001) planes were only ~0.6% of the average c lattice parameter.
Hardness of the high-entropy diborides was generally greater than the average hardness of the five individual constituent metal diborides.
Oxidation resistance was generally better than the average of individual components, with HEB#1 and HEB#7 maintaining shape at 1500 °C while TiB2 pulverized.
Revised Hume-Rothery size-difference factors based on lattice constants (δc) of 3.9% to 5.2% rationalized single-phase formation, whereas the non-single-phase specimen had δc ≈ 6.2%.
Minor secondary oxide phases ((Zr, Hf)O2) were observed in six specimens, and a secondary (Ti1.6W2.4)B4 phase was found in the W-containing specimen.
item.mechanism: The formation of high-entropy solid solutions is rationalized by a revised Hume-Rothery size-difference factor calculated from lattice constants rather than atomic radii; the rigid 2-D boron net constrains the metal layers, reducing the effective size mismatch (δa) and allowing entropy stabilization of the disordered solid solution despite larger atomic size differences in the c-direction.
item.limitations: The presence of porosity and oxide inclusions resulting from the HEBM procedure adversely affected hardness and oxidation resistance; MoB2 is metastable at room temperature and W2B5 starting powder has limited solubility; the study did not fully optimize microstructure for maximum property performance.
item.future_work: Further systematic investigation of hardness, oxidation resistance, and other properties is needed, particularly focusing on processing optimization to achieve fully-dense and oxide-free specimens and utilizing the large compositional design space to tailor protective oxide scales.
quotes: Greater than 92% of the theoretical densities have been generally achieved with largely uniform compositions from nanoscale to microscale.

Initial property assessments show that both the hardness and the oxidation resistance of these high-entropy metal diborides are generally higher/better than the average performances of five individual metal diborides made by identical fabrication processing.
